headline: Structure-aware methods map RNA hairpins, protein binding, and modification motifs
label: Rna Structure And Binding Methods
summary: Recent preprints and publications pair sequence-based RNA structure inference with curated binding, G-quadruplex, and modification resources.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference of RNA sequence and structure features from sequence alone, chemical probing, or direct sequencing signal, alongside curated resources for benchmarking them. RLMHelix scores helices from single sequences using language-model dependencies and thermodynamics and scans the human transcriptome for conserved structures. A DMS-based study quantifies RBP occupancy on RNA hairpins in human cells and links occupancy to decay. On the resource side, G4All provides experimentally confirmed G-quadruplex sequences with non-G4 controls and condition annotations, and RNAffinityDB compiles experimental RNA-protein binding affinities. A nanopore direct RNA sequencing study applies exponential population analysis to extract candidate motifs for pseudouridine, inosine, and m5C. What is new is the pairing of sequence-level inference with in-cell occupancy measurements and experimentally curated binding data, though the set is heterogeneous and the database and motif items do not model structure directly.
